metadata.title: LUNAVI simulated demo scenario (November 2026)
metadata.sunCriterion: Not modelled — the fixture's sunlight intervals are illustrative.
metadata.earthCriterion: Not modelled — the fixture's Earth line-of-sight intervals are illustrative.
metadata.referenceFrame: Not applicable — no geometry is computed in simulated mode.
metadata.ephemeris: Not applicable — no geometry is computed in simulated mode.
assumptions: All intervals are hand-authored, deterministic demo values in UTC.
Intervals are half-open [start, end): a window is covered only if the intervals contain every instant of it.
Outside each site's coverage the state is unknown and is never treated as visible.

The fixture's Earth intervals sit inside the period when Earth's disc is geometrically above a flat horizon at the south pole (about 17 Nov 01:00 to 30 Nov 14:00 UTC, 2026), computed with NAIF DE421 kernels; the obstruction times themselves are illustrative.
limitations: Simulated values are not NASA-verified lunar predictions and must not be used for planning.
Map positions are illustrative and are not lunar coordinates; no distances are shown.
No terrain model is used, so no azimuth, elevation or horizon angles are available in this mode.

events.summary: In this simulated scenario the Sun drops below the local horizon at Demo Point A at 08:00 UTC on 21 Nov and stays obstructed until 12:00 UTC on 25 Nov.
In this simulated scenario sunlight returns to Demo Point A at 12:00 UTC on 25 Nov, and Earth stays geometrically visible.
